definition: A 1.5B reinforcement-learning-trained mathematics model used in this archive as a teacher, and specifically as the weak-teacher case. In the test-time-scaling study it is the teacher whose advantage over the student exists only at small sampling budgets, which makes it the control showing that on-policy distillation's failure to expand the capability boundary does not depend on the teacher being uniformly stronger -- the same pattern appears whether the teacher leads everywhere or only at small K. It also appears in the token-agreement work. Neither source describes its training beyond the name.

evidence.note: Identifies degenerate agreement -- students reaching near-perfect token agreement with a teacher by looping while the response as a whole is broken -- and replaces the agreement objective with two directional mismatch corrections, one bounding runaway excess tokens and one injecting teacher-preferred mass at positions the student almost never samples.
evidence.title: Mismatch Matters: On-Policy Distillation Beyond Token Agreement

evidence.note: Evaluates on-policy distillation across sampling budgets from 1 to 1024 and finds it consistently improves accuracy at small budgets while losing to the untrained base model at large ones, so what it transfers is sampling efficiency rather than capability -- and off-policy distillation, tested the same way, does expand the boundary.
evidence.title: Towards Understanding On-Policy Distillation through the Lens of Test-Time Scaling

name: JustRL-DeepSeek-1.5B
